accent: General American, the way a warm American storyteller reads aloud
$comment: Who speaks with which voice, for each provider (docs/voice-bakeoff.md). `describe` is the character in a sentence: it goes into Gemini's style (3.8) or audio profile (3.1), and is what to listen for on every engine. ElevenLabs ids are premade voices (named beside each id); swap in Voice Library picks freely, and an id your account cannot use shows as a failed cell, never a failed run. Gemini names are its prebuilt voices. `party` is the heroes speaking ("you say"); it reads in the narrator's voice by default so no child is cast as a stranger's voice. Everyone speaks with `accent` (American: the game is for American children); Gemini is told it in each style, and the ElevenLabs voices are American premade voices, since an ElevenLabs voice's accent is the voice's own.

narrator.describe: A warm grown-up storyteller reading to eight-year-olds: unhurried, smiling, a little spooky on the quiet bits, never scary.

party.describe: The heroes themselves, read by the storyteller.

pib.describe: A bramble sprite the size of a teapot: earnest, quick, over-explains, offers you things you did not ask for.

mob.describe: A crowd of impatient treasure hunters shouting together.

faun.describe: A gentle faun gardener, soft-spoken and a little startled.

quill.describe: A griffin postmaster in glasses, flustered and squawky, far too busy.

madame_fenn.describe: A theatrical merfolk trader in a barrel on wheels who calls everyone darling.

seal_keeper.describe: An enormous ancient dragon with a slow, deep, kind voice, surprised by kindness.

sheeple.describe: A flock of sheeple answering all together, slightly out of step.

sheeple_middle.describe: The sheeple in the middle of the flock: earnest, a bit slow, very sure of the group.

sheeple_a.describe: One sheeple from the flock, eager to agree.

sheeple_b.describe: Another sheeple from the flock, very solemn about it.

traveler_a.describe: A chatty traveler at a roadside fire, enjoying the gossip.

traveler_b.describe: A second traveler, topping the first one's story.

travelers.describe: A ring of travelers all asking at once.

hessa.describe: Hessa Wren: a soup-tent host, warm and motherly, who says unsettling things kindly.

orin.describe: Orin, a steady older guide on the ice, practical and calm.

seren.describe: Seren, a curious young scholar, thoughtful and hopeful.

delivery.$comment: Sustained delivery for a whole line: the closed vocabulary of docs/voice-narration-plan.md §3. `tag` is the bracketed audio tag ElevenLabs v3/v4 and Gemini 3.1 read in the text; `style` is how the line should sound, in words, which Gemini 3.8 takes in its speechMetadata.style field and Gemini 3.1 in its director's notes. Models with neither (ElevenLabs v2, Flash) ignore delivery, which is part of what the bake-off shows.

whisper.style: whispering, but clearly enough to be heard across a room

grave.style: slow and grave, deep and kind

chorus.style: a group speaking together, slightly out of step

kindly.style: warm and kind, as if it were nothing at all

beats.$comment: Point-in-time events inside a line, written <sigh> or <long pause> in a script's text and never shown on screen. Each provider family writes them its own way: `eleven` for ElevenLabs v3/v4 (bracketed tags; no SSML), `elevenClassic` for v2 and Flash (SSML breaks for pauses, nothing else), `gemini` for Gemini 3.8 (angle-bracket vocal tags, the only text it does not speak aloud), `geminiPrompt` for Gemini 3.1 (bracketed tags). null means the family has no way to say it, and the beat is left out. Sources and the unverified ones are in docs/voice-bakeoff.md.
